details: Every composite number can be expressed uniquely as a product of prime numbers, up to the order of factors.
Prime factor tree visualization decomposes composite numbers iteratively into prime branches.
HCF(a, b) is the product of the smallest power of each common prime factor involved in the numbers.
LCM(a, b) is the product of the greatest power of each prime factor involved in the numbers.
For any two positive integers a and b: HCF(a, b) * LCM(a, b) = a * b.
evidence_or_examples: Relation HCF * LCM = a * b holds ONLY for two positive integers, not three.

details: Let p be a prime number. If p divides a^2 (where a is a positive integer), then p divides a.
evidence_or_examples: If 2 divides a^2, then 2 divides a; used as key lemma in irrationality proofs.

details: Assume the number is rational in lowest terms p/q where p and q are coprime integers (q != 0).
Derive that the prime factor divides both p and q, contradicting the coprime assumption.
evidence_or_examples: Proof that √2 is irrational
Proof that √3, √5, and 3 + 2√5 are irrational

details: The zeroes of a polynomial p(x) are the x-coordinates of the points where y = p(x) intersects the x-axis.
A polynomial of degree n can have at most n real zeroes.
Quadratic polynomial y = ax^2 + bx + c forms a parabola opening upwards if a > 0 and downwards if a < 0.
evidence_or_examples: A parabola intersecting x-axis at (-2, 0) and (4, 0) has zeroes -2 and 4.
Cubic graph cutting x-axis at 3 distinct points has 3 real zeroes.

details: For ax^2 + bx + c with zeroes α and β:
Sum of zeroes: α + β = -b/a = -(coefficient of x) / (coefficient of x^2)
Product of zeroes: αβ = c/a = (constant term) / (coefficient of x^2)
evidence_or_examples: For x^2 - 2x - 8, zeroes are 4 and -2: Sum = 2 = -(-2)/1; Product = -8 = -8/1.
Polynomial formation: p(x) = k[x^2 - (α + β)x + αβ].

details: For ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d with zeroes α, β, γ:
Sum of zeroes: α + β + γ = -b/a
Sum of products in pairs: αβ + βγ + γα = c/a
Product of zeroes: αβγ = -d/a
evidence_or_examples: For x^3 - 3x^2 + x + 1 with zeroes a-b, a, a+b: Sum = 3a = 3 => a = 1; Product = a(a^2 - b^2) = -1 => b = ±√2.

details: Standard form system: a1 x + b1 y + c1 = 0 and a2 x + b2 y + c2 = 0.
Intersecting lines (Unique solution / Consistent): a1/a2 != b1/b2
Coincident lines (Infinitely many solutions / Dependent Consistent): a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2
Parallel lines (No solution / Inconsistent): a1/a2 = b1/b2 != c1/c2
evidence_or_examples: 5x - 4y + 8 = 0 and 7x + 6y - 9 = 0 -> 5/7 != -4/6 => Intersecting at unique point.

details: Express one variable in terms of the other from one equation.
Substitute this value into the second equation to obtain a single-variable linear equation.
Multiply one or both equations by non-zero constants to equalize coefficients of one variable.
Add or subtract equations to eliminate that variable.

details: Discriminant D = b^2 - 4ac.
D > 0: Two distinct real roots: x = (-b ± √D) / (2a).
D = 0: Two equal real roots: x = -b / (2a).
D < 0: No real roots.
evidence_or_examples: 2x^2 + kx + 3 = 0 has equal roots when D = k^2 - 24 = 0 => k = ±2√6.
2x^2 - 3x + 5 = 0 has D = -31 < 0 => No real roots.

details: BPT (Theorem 6.1): If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, the other two sides are divided in the same ratio.
In ΔABC, if DE || BC, then AD/DB = AE/EC.
Converse (Theorem 6.2): If a line divides any two sides of a triangle in the same ratio, then the line is parallel to the third side.
evidence_or_examples: In ΔABC with DE || BC, AD = 1.5 cm, DB = 3 cm, AE = 1 cm => EC = 2 cm.
Trapezium ABCD with AB || DC: diagonals intersect at O => AO/BO = CO/DO.

details: Two triangles are similar if corresponding angles are equal and corresponding sides are proportional.
AAA (or AA): If two angles of one triangle are equal to two angles of another.
SSS: If three sides of one triangle are proportional to three sides of another.
SAS: If one angle equals one angle and the including sides are proportional.
evidence_or_examples: Girl 90 cm tall walking from 3.6 m lamp-post at 1.2 m/s: shadow x after 4 s => x/(x+4.8) = 0.9/3.6 = 1/4 => x = 1.6 m.

details: Line of Sight: Straight line drawn from observer's eye to target point.
Angle of Elevation: Angle between line of sight and horizontal baseline when looking UP.
Angle of Depression: Angle between line of sight and horizontal baseline when looking DOWN.
Angle of depression equals angle of elevation from observer object due to alternate interior angles.
evidence_or_examples: Pole 6 m high casts shadow 2√3 m => tan θ = 6/(2√3) = √3 => θ = 60°.
Circus artist climbing 20 m rope tied to pole top at 30° => sin 30° = AB/20 => pole height = 10 m.

details: A tangent to a circle touches the curve at exactly one point (point of contact).
Theorem 10.1: The tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact (OP ⊥ XY).
evidence_or_examples: From Q, tangent length = 24 cm, distance from center = 25 cm => radius r = √(25^2 - 24^2) = 7 cm.
Tangents drawn at the ends of a diameter are parallel because interior angles on same side sum to 180°.

details: Theorem 10.2: The lengths of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal (PQ = PR).
Tangents subtend equal angles at center and are equally inclined to line joining point to center.
evidence_or_examples: Parallelogram circumscribing a circle is a rhombus (AB + CD = AD + BC => AB = AD).
Concentric circles: chord of larger touching smaller is bisected at point of contact.

details: Sector: Region enclosed by two radii and an arc.
Arc length of sector angle θ: L = (θ / 360°) * 2πr
Area of sector angle θ: A = (θ / 360°) * πr^2
evidence_or_examples: Area swept by 14 cm minute hand in 5 min (θ = 30°): A = (30/360) * (22/7) * 196 = 154/3 cm^2.

details: Segment: Region bounded by a chord and an arc.
Area of minor segment = Area of sector - Area of inner triangle
Area of inner triangle in sector θ: (1/2) r^2 sin θ
evidence_or_examples: Chord subtends 60° with r = 15 cm: sector area = 117.75 cm^2, equilateral triangle area = 97.3125 cm^2 => minor segment = 20.4375 cm^2.
4 quadrants of radius 7 cm cut from 14 cm square: remaining area = 196 - 154 = 42 cm^2.

details: Total Surface Area of composite solid = Sum of exposed Curved Surface Areas (CSAs) of individual components.
Internal overlapping contact faces are excluded from TSA.
evidence_or_examples: Toy made of cone mounted on hemisphere (r=3.5 cm, total height 15.5 cm => cone h=12 cm, l=12.5 cm): TSA = CSA(cone) + CSA(hemisphere) = πrl + 2πr^2 = 214.5 cm^2.
Two cubes of volume 64 cm^3 (side 4 cm) joined end-to-end: cuboid l=8, b=4, h=4 => TSA = 2(32 + 16 + 32) = 160 cm^2.

details: Total volume of composite solid = Sum of individual volumes of component solids.

Gulab jamun cylinder with two hemispherical ends (r=1.4 cm, length 5 cm): total syrup volume for 45 pieces = 30% of total volume ≈ 338 cm^3.

details: Modal class: Class interval with maximum frequency f1.

details: P(E) = (Number of outcomes favorable to E) / (Total number of possible outcomes n(S)).
Probability range bounds: 0 <= P(E) <= 1.
Impossible event P(E) = 0; Certain event P(E) = 1.
Complementary events: P(E) + P(not E) = 1.
evidence_or_examples: Die thrown once: P(prime number {2,3,5}) = 3/6 = 1/2.
Drawing card from 52-card deck: P(face card {12 cards}) = 12/52 = 3/13.
Two dice thrown simultaneously: n(S) = 36 outcomes => P(sum 8) = 5/36.
